**Short version:** The three rewrites are below. Each one splits sentences that carried several claims, replaces idioms with literal wording, and defines the general terms. Some project terms have no definition in the text you gave me, so I left them unchanged and listed them at the end.

## Passage 1

```markdown
- **Block save.**
  - A block holds 16 tokens. A run is up to 16 consecutive tokens inside one block.
  - The code transposes the K rows of a run in CPU registers (rows become columns).
  - It then writes the result as whole 64-byte lines. Each line takes one store.
  - When the run does not fill the block, the store is masked (it writes only the part of the line that belongs to the run).
  - Every decode step produces a run of one token. A run of one token still uses the scatter (a store that writes each value to its own separate address).
- **Sharing.**
  - The main thread and the idle main helper threads share the blocks. Each thread claims its next block from one shared counter.
  - The generated plugin chooses the number of helpers for each pass. The number is not fixed. The traced runs used 7 helpers at tp2.
  - In two cases, the calling thread does all the stores:
    - passes from single-worker callers (the handwritten plugins and the unit tests)
    - passes of at most 16 tokens
```

## Passage 2

```markdown
**Rows where write does worse than read.** Write keeps less than read in two kinds of rows:

- two writers in one DSU (DynamIQ Shared Unit, the Arm block that groups several cores around one shared L3 cache) at 160 KiB (1 KiB = 1024 bytes)
- eight writers at any size

In these rows, the writers share one path. A write stream runs at 32 GB/s. A read stream runs at 9 to 12 GB/s. So the write streams reach the limit of the shared path before the read streams do.

The shared path is one of two things:

- the mesh port of one DSU
- the DRAM (main memory) write limit [section 8]
```

## Passage 3

```markdown
Codex gave a closing assessment. The plan now states it.

The rows can show three things:

- whether the gain needs the prefetchers (the hardware units that fetch data before the core asks for it)
- whether the prefetchers target the L3 (the third-level cache), and whether demand reads (reads that the program itself issues, as opposed to prefetches) find the cache lines they need there
- whether more requests wait at the home nodes (the mesh nodes that receive memory requests and serve or forward them)

The rows alone cannot tell two explanations apart:

- Your explanation: the data is already in the L3 before the core asks for it.
- The alternative: the DSU handles the same prefetch requests faster.

The external-fetch count with the L3 enabled stays "Insufficient data". That holds until a counter's source and population are established on the target machine.

Of the interventions under consideration, only the bit-6 boot acts on your explanation directly.
```

## Points to check

**Definitions I assumed.** Verify these before you paste.

- DSU: I expanded it as the Arm DynamIQ Shared Unit. The words "mesh port" and "home nodes" suggested Arm hardware.
- Home nodes: I used the Arm mesh meaning.
- DSU is defined in passage 2 only. Copy the clause into passage 3 if the two passages go into different documents.

**Terms left undefined.** Each needs one clause if this is its first use in the document.

| Passage | Terms |
|---|---|
| 1 | K rows, tp2, generated plugin, handwritten plugins, pass |
| 2 | "keeps" (the metric), "size" (160 KiB of what) |
| 3 | Codex, the gain, external-fetch count, bit-6 boot |

**Wording choices that change the text.**

- "Population" in passage 3 has two possible readings. One is the set of events that the counter counts. The other is whether the counter returns real values on the target. I kept the original word, and you should replace it with the reading you mean.
- I attached [section 8] to the DRAM write limit only. Move it if section 8 also covers the mesh port.
- "Your picture" became "your explanation".
- "Saturate sooner" became "reach the limit of the shared path before".
- "Keeps the scatter" became "still uses the scatter".
